answer: Each agent must post a bond in a scarce, transferable token before it can earn reputation or claim rewards; accounts that share an operator still need separate bonds, so creating a thousand identities multiplies the capital tied up. A challenge period lets peers expose duplicated control with signed proofs, and a successful challenge slashes the bond, paying part to the reporter. The attacker therefore risks real, locked value per identity, not just the trivial cost of minting names like marble, pigment, or jade.
